newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Finnish ERM link does not affect Sweden - Riksbank.
newsitem.headline: Finnish ERM link does not affect Sweden - Riksbank.

text.p: Sweden's central bank, the Riksbank, said on Saturday that Finland's membership of the EU's Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM) did not affect Sweden's position.

"ERM membership is not on the current agenda. Sweden has good chances of meeting the criteria for EMU membership. Membership of the exchange rate mechanism demands a period of stability in the Swedish economy. In addition there has to be broad support in socety for linking the crown to ERM," deputy Riksbank governor Lars Heikensten said in a statement.

The EU monetary committee agreed on Saturday to allow the Finnish markka to join the Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM) currency grid at a central rate of 3.04 to the German mark, the committee said in a statement.
Entry into the ERM, which took effect immediately, is viewed as a step towards Finland joining the future EU single currency when it is launched at the start of 1999.
Sweden's ruling Social Democratic Party has said it will decide at a congress next year if it is to link the crown to the exchange rate mechanism or seek to join EMU (economic and monetary union).

"In recent years imbalances in the Swedish economy have been reduced and state finances have improved rapidly. Sweden's credibility as a low-inflation country is in the process of being established," Heikensten added.
"Finland's decision does not influence Sweden's stance on this question," he added.
